Method of Attack: Injecting JavaScript into hacked WordPress sites to display a fake Q&A forum overlay with a link to a ransomware installer
Downloading a zip file containing obfuscated JScript that connects to a remote server to retrieve and decrypt a payload
Executing a PowerShell command extracted from a GIF file to run the Sodinokibi DLL for file encryption
Clearing victim's Shadow Volume Copies using PowerShell to prevent recovery
Impacted Systems: Windows systems (via PowerShell and DLL execution)
Attack Vector: Compromised WordPress sites with injected JavaScript overlay
User clicking on malicious download link in fake forum post
Execution of downloaded JScript and PowerShell commands
Indicators of Compromise: Injected JavaScript overlay displaying fake French Q&A forum post
Obfuscated JScript file with same name as zip
PowerShell command that deletes Shadow Volume Copies: Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy | ForEach-Object {$_.Delete();}
Ransom note directing victims to a Tor payment site
